candidates.change_summary: Replace the assignment to owner with a no-op (commented-out) so transferOwnership no longer updates owner.
Assign owner to the zero address instead of the provided _newOwner, changing resulting owner value after the call.
Assign owner to msg.sender (caller) rather than the provided _newOwner, causing owner to remain or revert to caller.
Assign owner to tx.origin instead of _newOwner, changing owner when proxied/calls differ.
Assign owner to a fixed constant address (0x000...1) rather than the provided _newOwner.
Remove the require check so onlyOwner no longer restricts execution (deleted require), allowing anyone to call transferOwnership and change owner.
Invert the require condition so it requires msg.sender != owner, allowing only non-owners to execute guarded functions and changing who can call transferOwnership.
Replace empty body of owned() with an assignment that sets owner to caller, changing state visible via owner after calling owned().
Change onlyOwner modifier to remove the requirement check, allowing any caller to execute guarded functions and thus potentially change owner when owned() is called.

Invert the ownership check so that only non-owners can execute guarded functions, allowing someone other than owner to call owned() and thereby change observable owner-related behavior if owned() modifies state.
Replace the owner assignment with a no-op (remove state change) so transferOwnership no longer updates owner.
Assign owner to tx.origin instead of the provided _newOwner, changing which address becomes owner after call.
Assign owner to msg.sender (already required by modifier) instead of _newOwner, preventing transfer to other addresses.
Remove the require check so anyone can call transferOwnership, changing who can successfully change owner.
Invert the require condition so only non-owners can call owner-only functions, altering who can perform transferOwnership.
